sections.title: Red oak
sections.text: Northern red oak is a large deciduous tree native to eastern North America. It typically grows about 15–23 m tall with a similarly broad crown. Its leaves have 7–11 sharply pointed lobes and turn reddish-brown in autumn.

sections.title: Acorns and food
sections.text: The rounded acorns are about 2–4 cm long and take two growing seasons to mature. They are edible after tannins are removed by leaching or boiling; raw acorns are astringent. The plate correctly shows pointed leaves, hanging catkins and a large acorn.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.text: Unlike evergreen Q. ilex and downy-leaved Q. pubescens, this North American oak has sharply bristle-tipped lobes. Its acorns mature over two seasons, unlike those of Q. ilex and Q. pubescens.
